title: Radical Rationality
coreMove: Carry the value scorecard across contexts while forcing every admired tactic to re-earn its place under current facts.
sourcePressure: The synthesis chapter distills the outsider mind-set across Murphy, Singleton, Anders, Malone, Graham, Stiritz, Smith, and Buffett without flattening them into one tactic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not create a generic outsider manifesto; every transfer must test whether the principle, not the visible tactic, fits the local constraints.

sourceAnchors.name: Tom Murphy, Henry Singleton, Bill Anders, John Malone, Katharine Graham, Bill Stiritz, Dick Smith, and Warren Buffett
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the synthesis must preserve the recurring operating logic of the earlier cases while keeping their differences alive.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Put the eight names beside each other and the sameness is not a tactic; it is a scorecard that keeps changing tools.

sourceAnchors.name: The Outsider's Mind-Set
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies Chapter 9 as Radical Rationality and pairs it with The Outsider's Mind-Set.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The outsider mind-set is not a costume; it is the habit of making every tool prove its economics again.

examples: personal productivity system copied from elsewhere

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: No more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'.
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: At least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human.
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: regional library system copying a no-branches digital strategy from a different city
exampleSpecs.audience: a library director under pressure to imitate a famous turnaround
exampleSpecs.stakes: closing small branches could harm the very patrons the system exists to serve
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily writes the borrowed tactic on one side of the table and the local patron-access scorecard on the other, then keeps only the digital scheduling principle and rejects branch closures.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: library card renewal forms stacked beside a tablet checkout dock

exampleSpecs.domain: manufacturing apprenticeship program tempted to copy decentralization from a larger plant
exampleSpecs.audience: a training director with new supervisors not ready for full local authority
exampleSpecs.stakes: badly copied autonomy could put apprentices near unsafe machines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien asks supervisors to predict which decisions they can own safely, then keeps decentralization only for tool ordering while centralizing machine-access rules.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lockout tag hanging from a lathe handle

exampleSpecs.domain: craft brewery copying buyback-like owner distributions while tanks need maintenance
exampleSpecs.audience: a minority owner who admires capital discipline but faces different constraints
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash returned too early could leave the cellar unable to meet demand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia compares the admired distribution tactic with tank-maintenance and demand data, then keeps the value scorecard but sends cash to the cellar because the local facts demand it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: condensation running down a fermenter beside a maintenance tag

exampleSpecs.domain: city procurement office adopting a private-company pruning rule
exampleSpecs.audience: a procurement lead deciding whether to cut supplier categories
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying private-sector focus could reduce resilience during emergency repairs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Luke one emergency repair miss to see that the copied pruning rule had killed supplier redundancy without improving value, so he rebuilds the scorecard around resilience and cost.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an emergency repair ticket stamped beside a deleted supplier list

exampleSpecs.domain: boutique investment office importing Berkshire-style autonomy for outside managers
exampleSpecs.audience: a family office COO mistaking trust language for governance
exampleSpecs.stakes: manager freedom without capital review can compound unnoticed risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Manon keep the long-term trust principle but add a quarterly capital review because local managers do not get to borrow the language of autonomy without the discipline.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: manager letters marked with colored risk tabs

exampleSpecs.domain: university athletics department copying a corporate scorecard for team funding
exampleSpecs.audience: an athletic director under pressure to become more businesslike
exampleSpecs.stakes: one imported metric would starve low-revenue teams that carry scholarship and compliance value
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What survives if the metric changes but the value question stays? Devon separates revenue, athlete welfare, and compliance before adapting the scorecard instead of copying the corporate one whole.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: scholarship forms tucked under a practice-court rental report

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: separate principle from visible tactic across cases
test borrowed management tools against local constraints
identify fake outsider traits detached from value logic
evaluate whether capital allocation means resources, authority, and attention beyond finance

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one borrowed tactic you admire and write the original problem it solved, your current problem, and the condition that would make the tactic fail here.
